Amsterdam UMC (location VUmc)
Department of Radiology

Examination: mpMRI Prostate (3T)
Date: 15 January 2025

Clinical Indication:
Elevated PSA (5.8 ng/mL) with rising trend. Previous biopsy negative. Evaluation for clinically significant prostate cancer.

Findings:
The prostate volume is calculated at 39.0 mL. The peripheral zone demonstrates a focal lesion in the left posterior mid-gland. On T2-weighted imaging, this area appears as a discrete, low-signal intensity region. Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) shows corresponding restricted diffusion with high signal on b1500 images and low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging reveals early, focal enhancement within this region. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous lesions are seen.

Impression:
1. PI-RADS v2.1 score 4 lesion in the left posterior mid-gland peripheral zone.
2. Prostate volume 39.0 mL; PSA density 0.15 ng/mL/mL.
3. Clinical T stage cT1c.
4. csPCa predicted probability 0.40801913

previous_notes.text: Patient presented for routine annual check-up. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable with a smooth, symmetric prostate. PSA was measured at 2.3 ng/mL, which is within normal limits for his age. No further urological investigation was indicated at this time, and the patient was advised to continue routine screening.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (April 2022):
Histological examination of the prostate tissue cores reveals benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis. No malignant glands are identified. The Gleason score is reported as 0+0, corresponding to ISUP Grade Group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is not present.

Summary:
The patient has undergone one previous biopsy which was negative for malignancy. The current clinical picture involves a rising PSA and a PI-RADS 4 lesion, prompting re-evaluation despite the prior negative histological finding.
